note: Persistent Memory layer for the A/B self-improving loop (Loop Engineering 2.0). The unit under test is 'an agent completing a task'. The Optimiser mutates the aot-USAGE STRATEGY below (not aot source); source-improvement ideas are logged to recommendations[] for human review.

scoring.note: Fixed across all rounds — never tuned by the loop (tuning weights to manufacture a win is the External-Reference-Ratchet trap). Composite in [0,1]. Margin = mean(aot) - mean(baseline). Gate keeps a strategy change only if margin improves AND the improvement exceeds the noise floor (pooled stdev across replicates).

steps: Add a premise atom stating the task and its givens.
Add one reasoning atom per dependent step (each depends on the prior), making intermediate results explicit.
Add a hypothesis atom for the candidate answer, depending on the reasoning chain.
Add a verification atom (--supports/--refutes) checking the hypothesis against the constraints/arithmetic.
Add a conclusion atom; run `aot analyze` and resolve any contradiction/weakest-link warning before finalising.
Read the final answer off the conclusion atom.

backlog.hypothesis: Cap atoms to premise+hypothesis+verification+conclusion (drop intermediate reasoning atoms) to cut trace tokens — tests whether the token-efficiency loss to baseline can be recovered without hurting correctness.
Run `aot analyze` and only finalise once zero contradictions/weakest-link warnings remain — trades tokens for trace quality + correctness.
On logic/CSP tasks, require a hypothesis atom per candidate solution and a refutes-verification for each constraint violation — should lift correctness on shift-rota-style tasks.
Force one verification atom per intermediate result (not just the final hypothesis) — should raise objective correctness on multi-step numeric tasks by catching propagation errors early.

recommendations.recommendation: Make verification adaptive rather than blanket per-step: trigger a verification atom only on steps flagged high-uncertainty or error-prone (e.g. numeric ops, unit conversions, branch points), instead of forcing one per intermediate result. H1's evidence shows mandatory per-step verification adds atom/token overhead and noise that outweighs the correctness it buys.

Do not mandate a hypothesis atom per candidate (H2 pattern). Instead, tighten the verification-atom contract so a 'refutes' polarity verification can prune/mark isRefuted only when it carries an attached external check (executable constraint eval / trace), rather than a self-asserted atom — grounding refutation in an independent verifier instead of added self-structure.

priorRuns.verdict: honest null — aot ties freeform on tasks easy enough that freeform also scores correct=true; aot's higher quality/trace washed out by correctness+efficiency weighting. See results/run-001.json.

priorRuns.suite: 6 tasks (adds acid-base delta-delta, infusion rate, 4x4 CSP)
priorRuns.verdict: aot DECISIVELY loses (margin -0.084 beyond noise 0.026). Baseline got the hard tasks correct too, so aot overhead is unrepaid cost. Finding: aot pays off only when the base model would otherwise be WRONG; a frontier model rarely errs on textbook multi-step problems, so that regime needs genuinely adversarial tasks, not just more steps. See results/run-002.json.

priorRuns.whyRetracted: Inflated by (1) rubric leakage: the reasoning-trace rubric described aot's own premise/reasoning/hypothesis/verification DAG, giving the aot arm a vocabulary bonus worth +0.451 of the margin; (2) asymmetric token accounting: aot traceTokens from export --token-count (~2000) vs baseline char/4 of raw JSON, undercounting aot's read-cost. The self-improvement loop's own critique pass caught this; v2 fixes both with identical weights and reverses the sign. See results/run-integration.json (SUPERSEDED banner).

priorRuns.unitUnderTest: THE aot<->sgt integration as a unit (aot+sgt interleaved vs RAW sgt), decontaminated
priorRuns.suite: 5 UNCONTAMINATED retrieval tasks over the real 8733-skill corpus (k8s-netpol, db-migration, oauth-refresh, cicd-cache, webhook-verify) — rubrics never name atoms/DAG/aot vocabulary
priorRuns.weightsNote: IDENTICAL to v1 — verdict corrected by fixing MEASUREMENT (decontamination + symmetric cost accounting + seeded joint judging + retry), not by tuning weights.
priorRuns.mutations: INT4-gap-gated-expand2 (margin -0.397, discarded) and INT5-refute-retain (margin -0.125 over 4/5 tasks after a usage-limit cutoff, discarded). Neither usage-strategy mutation helped.
priorRuns.verdict: RAW sgt retrieval BEATS the aot interleaving on uncontaminated tasks: margin -0.142 clears noise floor 0.045. 4/5 tasks negative (oauth -0.324, k8s -0.257, webhook -0.130, cicd -0.015; db-migration +0.015 tie). v2 is an INDEPENDENT clean negative on Fable 5, not a single-variable correction of v1. See results/run-integration-v2.json.
priorRuns.controlCaveat: v1 ran on Opus 4.8; v2 ran on Fable 5; tasks also differ (3 vs 5). So model + tasks + the two measurement fixes ALL changed — the sign-reversal is not attributable to measurement alone. The negative is still robust: v1's flaws are demonstrable by code inspection (leaky rubric, asymmetric tokens) so +0.221 is untrustworthy regardless of model, AND a weaker model (Fable 5) should by the run-002 mechanism FAVOR aot more, yet aot still lost -0.142.
priorRuns.mechanism: Frontier model + raw sgt excerpts already answers correctly and cites them (baseline correct~1, high quality/trace). The aot layer's route->advise->expand->judge->trace adds token+latency cost the composite charges (0.25 efficiency weight), and its added quality/trace does not exceed that cost when the baseline is already right. This is run-002's mechanism EXACTLY: aot is unrepaid wherever the baseline is already correct.
priorRuns.sgtRunNote: The `aot sgt run` one-shot (shipped, 566 tests green) cuts agent round-trips/latency (timeEff, 0.10 weight) but not the disclosed-excerpt token cost. ARGUED (not measured — the aot-with-sgt-run arm was never run) to be unable to flip a correctness-dominated composite; verified only as a functioning code-level optimization.

adversarialRun.question: Does aot beat raw sgt in its PREDICTED regime — retrieval MISSES (naive top-1 off-domain)?
adversarialRun.suite: 4 verified lexical-decoy miss tasks (db-index->openalex, rate-limit->storage buckets, dead-letter->outlook-email, conn-pool->bioservices); both arms free to re-search
adversarialRun.finding: HYPOTHESIS FALSIFIED as a general claim. aot does NOT reliably beat raw sgt even under retrieval misses: margin -0.100 within noise, correct-grounding 75% < 83%. A capable model told the top hit may be off-domain re-searches on its own and grounds as well/better, cheaper.
adversarialRun.narrowPocket: aot WON the single most-severe decoy (adv-dead-letter, email hijack): +0.123, correct-grounding 100% vs 67% — judge --refutes + refine worked exactly as the mechanism predicts, but only at extreme decoy severity; does not generalize.
adversarialRun.dataNote: 4/24 samples were StructuredOutput artifacts (symmetric, 2/arm, small n); discounting them does not flip the sign.

lastVerdict: THREE-EXPERIMENT CONVERGENCE (all negative for aot): run-002 textbook -0.084, run-integration-v2 uncontaminated retrieval -0.142, run-adversarial retrieval-miss -0.100 within noise (correct-grounding 75% < 83%). The aot epistemic layer over sgt is NOT repaid vs raw sgt + a capable frontier model, even in its predicted best regime; its value is a narrow pocket (most-severe retrieval decoys, e.g. dead-letter +0.123) too small to clear noise. Engineering conclusion: keep raw sgt retrieval as the default; invoke the aot verification layer only on DETECTED high-ambiguity retrievals, never by default. No further usage-level optimization is determinable — the negative is robust, mechanism understood, and reaching aot's pocket requires either extreme-decoy detection (an ambiguity gate) or a task regime the corpus+model don't naturally produce. PRIOR (now-superseded) note follows: run-integration-v2 (decontaminated, symmetric, INDEPENDENT clean negative on Fable 5): RAW sgt retrieval BEATS the aot interleaving, margin -0.142 > noise 0.045. The v1 +0.221 'win' was RETRACTED — its rubric leakage + asymmetric token accounting are demonstrable by code inspection so it is untrustworthy regardless of model (v1 ran Opus, v2 ran Fable + different tasks, so v1->v2 is NOT a controlled A/B; the negative stands because a weaker model should favor aot more yet aot still lost). Caught by the loop's own critical-evaluation pass. CONVERGENCE: across run-001 (tie), run-002 (-0.084), and run-integration-v2 (-0.142), the invariant is that the aot epistemic layer is unrepaid whenever a frontier model is ALREADY correct — which good sgt retrieval on answerable tasks always is. aot's value regime requires base-model-WRONG or retrieval-MISS; usage-strategy mutations cannot reach it, and tuning weights to reach it is the External-Reference-Ratchet trap (forbidden). No further usage-level optimization is determinable without changing the task regime or the ranker (a different experiment, not this loop).
